column1: # rust-targets.tsv — which rustc every target we ship to actually has.
# THIS IS DATA, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING. It used to be a comment block in
# rust-vendor-tarball.sh next to a hardcoded MSRV="1.92", which is two statements
# of one fact: the prose explained that the floor is the lowest rustc among the
# shipping targets, and the constant asserted what that came to. Nothing checked
# that the two agreed, so the day a target moved, the comment would describe a
# floor the script did not use.
# Now the floor is DERIVED: rust-vendor-tarball.sh takes the minimum rustc over
# the rows marked `ship`, and watch-redumper-gui.yml compares upstream's declared
# rust-version against that same number. One fact, one place.
# Cross-check when this was introduced (2026-07-19): the derived minimum is 1.92,
# which is exactly what the constant said. The rewrite reproduces the known value
# rather than quietly changing it.
# `ship` vs `out` is the decision recorded on 2026-07-19: when a future release
# raises the floor, the affected target is switched OFF for the NEW version and
# the last package built for it stays in the repo and keeps being delivered. A
# row moving ship -> out is that switch. It does NOT mean "broken"; it means
# "frozen at the last version it could build".
# ⚠️ These numbers are MEASURED in clean containers, not read off a distro's
# website, and they are only as fresh as the `measured` column. An earlier note
# claimed trixie-backports had no newer rustc -- that was wrong, and it was wrong
# in a public upstream issue too. Re-measure before trusting a row that is old.
